key_concepts: Simple machines are devices that make work easier and faster.
A wedge is a double inclined plane sharpened to an end.
A wedge can separate objects or cut wood.
Levers have three classes: first-class, second-class, and third-class.
A seesaw, crowbar, scissors, and pliers are first-class levers.
A nutcracker and wheelbarrow are second-class levers.
A fishing rod, stapler, and baseball bat are third-class levers.
Inclined planes include ladders and stairs and help move loads with less effort.
Wheel and axle examples include doorknobs, car steering wheels, and rollers.
Pulleys are used to raise or lower loads, such as flagpoles and construction materials.
Screws are used in objects such as bulbs and bottle caps.
Teeth are wedges because they can cut objects.
